title: The Will of Saint Alder's
premise: When a letter arrives confessing to the murder of Saint Alder's beloved matriarch, Edith Voss, postmarked a full day after her funeral, Juniper Nystrom realizes the town convicted the wrong man years ago. Following a trail of misfiled taxi receipts, he discovers the 'dead' witness, Ruth Calloway, is alive and hiding in plain sight as the hospice nurse who tended Edith's final days. As Juniper and Edith's estranged grandson, Elias, unravel the Voss family's tangled inheritance, they uncover that Edith dictated her own confession before dying to protect Ruth from her son's violence. In the end, Juniper must choose between exposing a truth that will shatter Saint Alder's or honoring the will of a dead woman who loved the wrong people the right way.
about_author: Isandro Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former small-town records clerk who spent a decade listening to a town's secrets through a police scanner. The Will of Saint Alder's is his third novel and first mystery.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Towns
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. We meet him on a slow night shift, cataloging dispatch logs with obsessive precision, a man who has made invisibility an art form. A call comes in from the Voss estate, cut short. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine and its quiet loneliness.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A day after Edith Voss's funeral, a confession letter arrives at the taxi company addressed to 'whoever keeps the records.' The postmark is impossible—it's dated after her death. Juniper pockets it instead of reporting it. Emotional beat: the first crack in his ordered world.

chapters.title: What the Town Agreed to Forget
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He digs through old dispatch logs and finds a call from the Voss house seven years ago, the night a handyman was convicted of murder and a witness named Ruth Calloway reportedly drowned. Emotional beat: dread as patterns emerge in the files.

chapters.title: The Grandson Who Came Back
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Edith's estranged grandson arrives to settle the estate, resentful of the grandmother who cut him off. He notices the taxi company's dispatcher asking strange questions about his family. Emotional beat: grief tangled with old wounds.

chapters.title: A Nurse Named Nobody
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Following Edith's final-year taxi receipts, Juniper traces a hospice nurse who signed in under three different names. The description matches Ruth Calloway, dead seven years. Emotional beat: the thrill of a hunt waking something dormant in him.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Will
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The will is read: Edith leaves nearly everything to an unnamed 'keeper of my last confession.' The family is furious; the lawyer is evasive. Elias realizes the confession letter Juniper holds may be the inheritance itself. Emotional beat: avarice and suspicion dividing a family.

chapters.title: Receipts and Ruin
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Someone ransacks the dispatch office looking for the letter. Juniper hides the original and hands over a decoy. His boss, Marla, quietly covers for him—revealing she's known more than she ever said. Emotional beat: found family solidifying under threat.

chapters.title: Seven Years Underwater
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias investigates the drowning that never happened, finding his father's fingerprints all over the cover-up. The man his family convicted, Denny Okafor, is still in prison. Emotional beat: shame as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Woman at the End of Route 9
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper tracks the nurse to a cottage outside town and comes face to face with Ruth Calloway, alive and terrified. She refuses to talk but warns him: 'Edith wrote what Edith wanted written.' Emotional beat: awe and fear in equal measure.

chapters.title: What Edith Dictated
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Flashback to Edith's final weeks: her son Martin's violence, her decision to confess to a crime she witnessed but couldn't stop, and her love for Ruth. Emotional beat: love against duty, rendered in a dying woman's voice.

chapters.title: The Son Who Watched
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Martin Voss confronts Elias about the letter, and Elias sees his father's guilt plainly for the first time. Martin offers him money to walk away. Emotional beat: the seduction and rot of complicity.

chapters.title: Misfiled
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Marla reveals the taxi company has been quietly ferrying Ruth to and from the Voss estate for years—Edith's standing order, paid in cash. Juniper realizes the whole town's silence was bought, one ride at a time. Emotional beat: disillusionment with the town he served.

chapters.title: Denny Okafor's Letters
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper visits Denny in prison, who has spent seven years writing letters no one answered—to the taxi company, among others. Juniper finds one of his own unanswered letters in the files. Emotional beat: guilt as a mirror.

chapters.title: The Standing Order
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias finds his grandmother's ledger: payments, dates, and a final entry the night she died. The timeline doesn't match the confession letter's postmark—someone mailed it after her death, deliberately. Emotional beat: the mystery pivots from what to who.

chapters.title: Martin's Version
chapters.summary: Martin's POV. Martin admits he knew Ruth was alive and let Denny burn for it, believing he was protecting the family name. He threatens Juniper and Elias with everything he has. Emotional beat: a villain who thinks he's the last honest man.

chapters.title: Burning the Records
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The dispatch office is set ablaze; Marla is hurt pulling Juniper's logbooks from the fire. The town's paper memory is ash, but Juniper has memorized the one entry that matters. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Ruth Decides
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth, seeing the fire as the end of hiding, chooses to testify—for Denny, for Edith, and against the family that caged her. She gives Juniper the missing piece: Martin mailed the letter himself to smoke out the will's beneficiary. Emotional beat: courage as a choice, not a feeling.

chapters.title: The Keeper of the Confession
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. At the probate hearing, Juniper presents the letter and the ledger. The will's 'keeper' clause names whoever preserved the confession in good faith—Juniper himself. Emotional beat: the invisible man made suddenly, unbearably visible.

chapters.title: What the Town Owes
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Denny's exoneration hearing; the town splits between denial and reckoning. Marla, the lawyer, and old customers testify to the standing orders. Emotional beat: a community confronting its own complicity.

chapters.title: Martin's Long Night
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Cornered, Martin flees to the Voss estate; Elias and Juniper confront him in the house where it all began. Martin's confession is extracted not by force but by Elias refusing to be his son any longer. Emotional beat: breaking a bloodline's curse.

chapters.title: The Will of Saint Alder's
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The estate is settled: Denny freed, Ruth's name cleared, and Edith's house turned into a home for the hospice workers she relied on. Juniper keeps only one thing—her pen. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as responsibility.

chapters.title: Whoever Keeps the Records
chapters.summary: Juniper and Elias's alternating POV, closing scene. A year later, Juniper still works nights, but the dispatch office is now a de facto town archive, and Elias brings him coffee at 3 a.m. A new letter arrives, postmarked tomorrow. Emotional beat: found family, and the promise that some stories never quite file themselves away.
